sources.title: Marina Silva: biography, mandates, ministerial leave and return on 1 April 2026
sources.findings: Read Chamber biography: federal term 2023–2027, sworn February 1, 2023, ministerial leave from February 3 and resumed April 1, 2026. History degree and specialization are different qualifications. City council 1989–1991 and state assembly 1991–1995 precede Senate service. External-mandate rows do not fully describe party changes or continuous active Senate service during ministerial leave.

sources.title: Marina Silva: active federal deputy, REDE–SP, 2023–2027 term
sources.findings: Read current Chamber profile: active REDE–SP federal deputy; civil name Maria Osmarina Marina da Silva Vaz de Lima, birthday February 8, 1958, birthplace Rio Branco, Acre. This current institutional record overrides stale minister biographies. No personal contact details reproduced; no form submitted.

sources.title: Marina Silva: former senator profile, education and mandates
sources.findings: Read Senate identity, education and mandate tables. Senate terms 1995–2003 and 2003–2011 differ from uninterrupted attendance; ministerial leave is retained. Year-level dates are used rather than inventing exact accession days. Specialized study is not converted into a masters degree or PhD.

sources.title: PSB nominates Marina Silva: 20 August 2014 report and biographical background
sources.findings: Read Fernanda Calgaro’s August 20, 2014 UOL report: PSB nomination following Campos’s death, Albuquerque running mate and remaining coalition ratification step. Biography supports rubber-community childhood, literacy education, 1984 history graduation, union work, earlier elections and policy conflicts. Nomination, registration, polling forecasts and election victory are not interchangeable; no presidential victory claimed.

sources.title: Senators react to Marina Silva’s resignation request, 13 May 2008
sources.findings: Read Agência Senado’s May 13, 2008 report. Silva submitted a resignation request that afternoon and a Senate return was prospective in the report. Later return is corroborated by official career records; no assertion that all formal procedures or Senate resumption happened May 13. Senators’ praise is opinion, not independent proof of policy success.

sources.title: TSE unanimously approves REDE registration, 22 September 2015
sources.findings: Read UOL’s September 22, 2015 account of TSE’s 7–0 registration approval. The 2013 rejection concerned insufficient validated support signatures. Party-building initiative and later legal registration are separated. No claim to have read the full original court judgment or checked every signature.

sources.title: Official photo account: Marina Silva sworn in as environment minister on 1 January 2023
sources.findings: Read original Palácio do Planalto Flickr caption: January 1, 2023 swearing-in in Brasília, photographer Ricardo Stuckert/PR, uploaded January 13. This documents the event rather than the departmental handover ceremony on January 4. Caption read does not constitute viewing image pixels. Clicked the licence link, which resolves to CC BY 2.0.

sources.title: Formal ministerial departure and Capobianco appointment, 1 April 2026
sources.findings: Read Agência Estado’s April 1, 2026 dispatch via UOL: formal departure in DOU Extra and Capobianco’s formal appointment. April 1 is distinct from advance March 31 announcements. Candidate office was undecided in that historical report; subsequent Senate candidacy and defeat are established by the electoral court. No claim to have read the complete DOU issue.

sources.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de São Paulo
sources.title: 2026 São Paulo Senate election: final totals and two elected senators
sources.findings: Read TRE-SP’s October 4, 2026 report, updated October 5, with all precincts counted. Silva fourth, 7,862,400 votes and 18.12%; Derrite and Prado won the two seats. These are valid candidate-vote shares, not shares of individual electors; there is no Senate runoff. No personal re-count of ballots or certificate-of-election audit.

sources.title: Marina Silva: 2007 Champions of the Earth, Policy Leadership
sources.findings: Read UNEP’s 2007 Champions of the Earth profile and Policy Leadership classification. Its conservation/community-livelihood and cross-government assessment supports award context. Historic praise and then-current deforestation estimates are not presented as current measurements, independent causal proof or an achievement by Silva alone.

sources.publisher: Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima
sources.title: COP31 forest-policy panel with federal deputy Marina Silva, 12 November 2026
sources.findings: Read MMA’s COP31 report published November 13 and updated November 14. Actual panel occurred November 12 and included federal deputy Silva, minister Capobianco and other officials. Roadmap delivery was Capobianco’s, not Silva’s personal act. Zero deforestation by 2030 is a target, not accomplished zero; agency statistics were not independently reconstructed.

sources.title: Jéssica Maes interviews Marina Silva at COP31 on 14 November; published 17 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Jéssica Maes/Folhapress interview via Jornal de Brasília, published November 17, 2026, recounting November 14 in-person interview in Antalya. Reviewed substantive questions on climate-emergency framework, scientific committee, multi-level governance and fossil-fuel transition. A forthcoming Stiell meeting is not proof it occurred. Potential climate-authority role and ministry return remain speculation, not appointment. Loose year-end deputy wording is superseded by Chamber’s 2023–2027 term.
